newsitem.title: COMOROS: Seven seats undecided in Comoran elections.
newsitem.headline: Seven seats undecided in Comoran elections.

text.p: Parliamentary elections in the Comoro Islands this week decided 36 of the 43 seats in the federal assembly, leaving seven for a second round of voting on Sunday, the interior minister said on Wednesday.

The minister, Said Mohamed Said Hassane, said on state radio that the ruling National Rally for Development now had an absolute majority in parliament but did not give a breakdown of who had won the 36 seats.
By Monday, one day after first-round voting, the ruling party had won 26 seats, against four for independents and two for the Islamist National Front for Justice.

The main opposition alliance, the Forum for National Recovery, boycotted the vote in the former French colony, saying it wanted elections for a constituent assembly, a revision of electoral registers and a new independent electoral commission.
The second round on Sunday will be a contest between the top two candidates in cases where no candidate won an absolute majority in the first round.
For five of the seven remaining seats, the ruling party candidates face independents. In the other two they face candidates from the Islamist group.

The minister said the turnout in the first round was more than 70 percent but independent observers were sceptical. They say that half an hour before some polling stations closed in the capital Moroni, no more than 10 percent of people had voted.

"The two lessons to be drawn from the first round are that people went to the polls in force and secondly they decided to give President (Mohamed) Taki an absolute majority to carry out his recovery policy," Hassane said.
"People have finished paving the way to Rehemani," he added. Rehemani, Taki's slogan, is Swahili for "World of Wonders".
Taki won six years as president in elections held in March.
